recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core FHIR follow-up is needed unless a future work-group decision changes event-status semantics.
issue_request: FHIR-24562 was a Published/Persuasive technical correction asking that the Event Status entered-in-error definition stop referencing cancelled, which is not in the event-status value set, and instead reference stopped.
initial_application: Jira records GH#e4c3d40ead, and commit e4c3d40ead62746c198548b46242039e7e71c208 changed source/event/event-spreadsheet.xml from cancelled to stopped for the entered-in-error definition. The same historical commit also made analogous Request and SupplyDelivery status wording corrections.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists event in the active [logical] section, placing the event logical model and its generated terminology artifacts in current build scope. The current event spreadsheet and CodeSystem source already contain stopped and define entered-in-error as pointing to stopped. A same-day Zulip implementers thread raised the missing-cancelled-code problem and confirmed current/R4 wording should use stopped; community searches found no later conflicting FHIR-core decision.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because the current build-scope source already implements the Jira decision.
